card.summary: No free tier in use: 'All of our premium packages support posting, but some servers are read-only (free.xsusenet.com is no longer in use).'

free_tier.stated: No free tier in use: 'All of our premium packages support posting, but some servers are read-only (free.xsusenet.com is no longer in use).'
free_tier.notes: No price quoted; the pricing page was not read.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published; the unit is the article.

egress.terms: Plan-based; the only ceiling named on the page read is the connection count.

record.interface_detail: NNTP reader, standard commands; the page lists the full refusal set a client meets at connect and at article fetch.
record.chaining: A shorter-retention spool is the wrong primary for a 1 TiB/month archive and the right fill for recent content; 1100 days is the only day count among the providers in this set that publishes one.

limits.value: 'Too Many Connections' is a named refusal; the plan's connection count is the ceiling
posting is allowed on premium packages and refused with '440 Posting Not Allowed' where it is not

record.limits_note: This is the only provider in the set whose documentation lists the connection-level refusals next to the article-level ones, which is what a client needs to tell 'wrong password' from 'article gone'.
record.binding_note: At 1100 days the spool is the shortest published retention here, so a client pulling older releases meets 430 far more often than a connection or byte limit.

identity_cost.detail: Paid client-area account with email and card; usenet credentials are separate from the client-area login, which the KB calls out explicitly.

record.reliability_note: Nothing past 1100 days exists on this spool; the KB warns that client-area credentials are not usenet credentials, which is a common first-hour failure; a 503 is an overload rather than a credential problem.
record.confidence_note: Every string and the retention figure are the vendor's own knowledge-base page. No probe was run.

evidence.proved: The refusal set: '502 Authentication Error / 482 Invalid username or password'; '440 Posting Not Allowed'; '480 Authentication Required'; '423 Bad Article Number or 430 No Such Article Found' with 'Our retention is limited to 1100 days'; '503 Service Unavailable ... possibly due to maintenance or overload'; 'Too Many Connections'. Also 'Your email address and password for a user area are NOT your Usenet credentials.'
Connection-count sizing: 'Set connections to what your plan actually allows ... Going over what the plan permits gets connections refused.'

record.notes: Potential failure points: the connection cap, the 1100-day wall, or the credential split between client area and NNTP. The credential split is the one that breaks a first-hour setup; the 1100-day wall is the one that breaks an archive pull. Both are documented.

extras.failure_angle: credential split and a published retention wall
extras.account_states: 482 invalid credentials or expired account ('ensure your account is still active and hasn't expired'); 480 auth required; 503 service unavailable; 440 posting refused

card.summary: The service is shut down. 'XS Usenet has shut down - but your Usenet service continues without interruption. All accounts have been moved to EasyUsenet.' The...

free_tier.stated: The service is shut down. 'XS Usenet has shut down - but your Usenet service continues without interruption. All accounts have been moved to EasyUsenet.' The website and ordering system are closed.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; no per-object cap is published; the unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, approximately 750 KB by convention, so 1 TiB of monthly transfer corresponds to roughly 1.4 million article…

retention.stated: Not applicable: no new accounts are sold. Existing accounts keep their expiry date on the EasyUsenet infrastructure.

egress.terms: Not applicable; the ordering system is closed

record.interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563. No HTTP or object API exists for the download path, which is driven through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav.
record.chaining: Nothing composes: the capacity moved to EasyUsenet, which is the Abavia brand a client should price instead.
record.limits_note: No limits apply to a service that no longer signs up customers. The last published terms were a soft 5 TB/month ceiling on unlimited plans with speed cut to 40 Mbit above it, per the r/usenet map.
record.binding_note: Nothing binds because nothing is sold. A reader who needs this capacity must go to EasyUsenet, which inherited the accounts.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is closed. Existing credentials were migrated unchanged to reader.easyusenet.com.

record.reliability_note: Shut down after 15 years, citing staff shortages; accounts moved to EasyUsenet with the same username and password and a new hostname. The VPN product was suspended and set to close on August 31, with refunds for unused time.
record.confidence_note: The shutdown notice is the vendor's own page, read. The fetch reported no upstream status, so the page content is the evidence rather than an HTTP code.

evidence.proved: 'XS Usenet has shut down'; 'All accounts have been moved to EasyUsenet'; new server reader.easyusenet.com; 'Since starting in 2009 as the first freemium Usenet provider'
Xsusenet listed as an Abavia reseller with 'soft limits (5tb per month) ... above 5TB speed will be capped to 40Mbit'

record.notes: The interesting part is the epitaph: the first freemium Usenet provider in 2009 is gone in 2026, and its free-tier model went with it. That is the direction of travel for the debrid main question.
